creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 14, item 2.

These seven builtins compute in float64, so int inputs above 2^53 come back rounded while `type_of` still says `int`:

```rad
xs = [1792183561123456789, 1792183561123456790]
print(min(xs), max(xs))   // 1792183561123456768 twice, equal to neither input
print(sum(xs))            // 3584367122246913536, exact is ...579
print(floor(xs[0]))       // 1792183561123456768 (same for ceil, round, clamp)
```

Reproduces on main; `rad check` is clean. Epoch nanoseconds are the common case: a tracing CLI took `min()` of span start times, every span offset came out up to ~256 ns wrong, and the root span printed at `-0.0`. `rad docs min` says it "returns `int` if all inputs are integers", which holds for the type but not the value.

Fix: compare and add as int64 when every input is an int, and return an int argument unchanged from `round`/`floor`/`ceil`. `sum` of large ints can then overflow int64 instead; decide whether that errors (see bugfixes `a_sBSZN4IY`).

Where: `core/funcs.go` - `extractMinMaxNums` returns `[]float64` (:2048) for `math.Min`/`math.Max` (:1275, :1294); `sum` accumulates in float64 (:1074); `clamp` compares floats (:1318); `round`/`ceil`/`floor` read `GetFloat` (:1236, :1254, :1261).
title: min, max, sum, clamp, round, floor and ceil lose precision on ints above 2^53
